audits.question: Check the entry's oracle-bone language, divination and royal-ancestor coupling using an inscription/corpus or scholarly passage; do not turn one archive's genre into all Shang speech or belief.
audits.entry_locator: lines 24-25 (evidence-ladder row 1); line 49; lines 57-69 (divination workflow); lines 73-79 (ancestors and Di)
audits.entry_claim: Late-Shang oracle inscriptions are the evidence class of 'Royal concerns, diviners, dated charges, named recipients of ritual' with the attached limit 'Formulaic, selective, and elite-centered; not a complete spoken-language sample or myth handbook' (lines 24-25); the late-Shang oracle corpus is 'the earliest extensive, securely readable Chinese writing corpus' (line 49); record components (preface, charge, prognostication, verification) are analytical categories, not mandatory slots, and positive/negative paired charges 'occur but are not an invariant template' (lines 59-65); charges connect royal ancestors and Di with illness, harvest, settlement and enemy action (lines 73-79).
audits.source_citation: de Bary and Bloom, eds., Sources of Chinese Tradition, 2nd ed., vol. 1 (New York: Columbia University Press, 1999), pp. 8, 11-12, 'Oracle-Bone Inscriptions of the Late Shang Dynasty', publisher-permitted web reproduction at Columbia University Asia for Educators (entry-cited source DB99)
audits.source_locator: page introduction paragraph; inscriptions nos. 8, 9A/9B, 19A/19B, 20A/20B, 22A/22B, 23, 24A/24B (DB99 pp. 8, 11-12); companion page pp. 9, inscription no. 15A/15B (see corroboration field)
audits.source_excerpt: The inscriptions give us a highly selective record of some of the concerns and events that were relevant to the elite class of the Shang kingdom.
audits.retrieval_method: FetchURL (HTTP GET) of the Asia for Educators web reproduction of DB99 pp. 8, 11-12; page main text extracted in full. Mediator inspected: English translation in the de Bary/Bloom sourcebook as republished by Columbia's Asia for Educators; no oracle-bone photographs, rubbings or Chinese graphs were inspected, so this is a translated selection, not the unread physical primary corpus.
audits.basis: Retrieved text matches every bounded element: (1) genre limit verbatim ('highly selective record ... relevant to the elite class'), grounding 'formulaic, selective, elite-centered' and entailing 'not a complete spoken-language sample'; (2) 'the earliest written records of Chinese civilization ... China's written history begins with these inscriptions around 1200 BCE', consistent with line 49's narrower 'earliest extensive, securely readable' framing; (3) named diviners Gu, Zheng, Que with dated crack-making prefaces (yiwei day 32, renzi day 49, guichou day 50); (4) paired positive/negative charges 19A/19B, 20A/20B, 22A/22B alongside unpaired records 8 and 23, matching 'occur but are not an invariant template'; (5) royal-ancestor/Di coupling: Father Yi and Grandfather Di(ng) 'harming the king' in illness charges, Di approving settlement building, 'It is Di who is harming our harvest', 'it is Di who orders (the Fang) to make disaster'. The companion childbearing inscription 15A additionally shows all four components in one record, including the king's prognostication and a verification recording failure ('it was not good; it was a girl'), supporting lines 63-64.
audits.coupling_implication: The entry's operational coupling 'scheduled ritual -> restricted utterance -> authorized interpretation -> durable record -> later ancestral memory' (line 68) is evidenced as a design abstraction, not a Shang doctrine: the retrieved records show scheduling (cyclical day), named diviner/king interpretation, and inscribed outcomes tied to ancestors and Di, but the source itself states the archive is a selective elite record, so the coupling must be modeled as royal-workflow-specific and never generalized to all Shang speech or belief.
audits.limits: English translation inspected only; graphs, transcription quality and bone provenance unchecked, so no graph-reading or dating claim is verified. 'Not a myth handbook' was not directly asserted by the source; it follows from the selectivity statement only as an absence of evidence. DB99's Wu Ding reign dates (r.1198-1189 BCE) are the handout's chronology and are not adopted (entry line 41 reserves this). Language-family affiliation (line 46, Sinitic/Sino-Tibetan via BS14) was NOT tested this session: BS14 was not retrieved, and this passage cannot support it. The page is a publisher-permitted web reproduction with DBQ apparatus, not the print edition; page numbers carried from the reproduction's own citation line.
audits.corroboration_note: Second entry-cited DB99 page (p. 9) fetched same session; inscription 15A/15B retrieved: 'Crack-making on jiashen (day 21), Que divined: Lady Hao's ... childbearing will be good.' (Prognostication:) The king read the cracks ... (Verification:) ... on jiayin (day 51), she gave birth; it was not good; it was a girl.' Directly supports the component table (lines 60-64), the Lady Hao living designation (line 162), and stem-day coupling (lines 137, 142); its single non-paired form further shows the template is not invariant.

audits.question: Check one bronze/jade, dressed-rank or ritual-vessel terminology claim and its period: separate Shang object evidence, Zhou institutions and later transmitted ritual prescriptions.
audits.entry_locator: line 116 (bi/cong = Heaven/Earth formula from transmitted Zhouli, Chun Guan Zong Bo); relatedly line 99 (fixed 9/7/5 vessel-rank ladder 'must not be treated as excavated laws for all periods')
audits.entry_claim: The bi disc = Heaven / cong tube = Earth correspondences 'come from the transmitted Zhouli (Chun Guan Zong Bo: "以蒼璧禮天，以黃琮禮地"; transcription checked 2026-10-17), a later prescriptive text; they still need a dated textual argument before being made the original meaning of every Neolithic or Shang specimen' (line 116); likewise any fixed numerical vessel/rank prescription needs a dated text and regional assemblage rather than counting as excavated law (line 99).
audits.source_citation: Zhouli 周禮, 'Chun Guan Zong Bo' 春官宗伯, Wikisource traditional-Chinese transcription (entry-cited source URL), classical transmitted ritual text; no critical edition consulted
audits.source_locator: Da Zong Bo office description: '以玉作六器，以禮天地四方' clause (the bi/cong formula), same office '以九儀之命正邦國之位' nine-grade ladder and '以玉作六瑞，以等邦國' six jade rank-tablets; Si Fu 司服 office ranked garments; Da Bu 大卜 divination-bureau clauses
audits.source_excerpt: 以玉作六器，以禮天地四方：以蒼璧禮天，以黃琮禮地
audits.retrieval_method: FetchURL (HTTP GET) of the Wikisource transcription; full page main text extracted. Mediator inspected: community Wikisource classical-Chinese transcription (traditional characters); no modern translation, critical edition or collated apparatus inspected in this retrieval.
audits.basis: Verbatim match: the retrieved transcription contains '以玉作六器，以禮天地四方：以蒼璧禮天，以黃琮禮地，以青圭禮東方，以赤璋禮南方，以白琥禮西方，以玄璜禮北方', exactly the quotation entry line 116 attributes to Chun Guan Zong Bo, confirming the attribution half of the claim as transmitted text. The same retrieved office text is prescriptive in genre ('以禮天地四方' is an instruction for sacrificial use of six jade types) and additionally contains '以九儀之命正邦國之位：壹命受職，再命受服，三命受位，四命受器...', '以玉作六瑞，以等邦國：王執鎮圭，公執桓圭...', and the Si Fu graded garment code, evidencing that numerical rank/garment/vessel prescriptions are Zhouli-style transmitted prescription material, which is exactly the entry's reason for warning against reading such ladders as excavated law (lines 99, 128, 152). The Da Bu/Gui Ren/Zhan Ren bureau clauses also show a later institutionalized divination administration, usefully contrasted with the Shang workflow of R6-06-A.
audits.coupling_implication: Period separation is preserved in the reference base: Shang-side evidence stays object-level (the Shanghai Museum record retrieved as corroboration attests the Fu Hao kneeling jade pendant's excavation context and late Shang attribution but carries no Heaven/Earth meaning claim), Zhou institutional material is available where dated, and the bi=Heaven / cong=Earth formulas and numeric ladders are carried as transmitted prescriptive text that must never be projected back onto Neolithic or Shang specimens in lore handoffs.
audits.limits: Support is partial by design: the transcription verifies wording and prescriptive genre, not the Zhouli's compilation date or the claim that it is 'later' than the specimens — that dating rests on scholarship not retrieved this session (Britannica topic page HTTP 403; Met object 44783 and Timeline essay HTTP 429 on repeated attempts; access left unresolved rather than inferred). The Wikisource page has no critical apparatus, so textual variants are unexamined; classical Chinese was inspected without a translation this session. The non-projection half of the claim (what Neolithic/Shang specimens did or did not mean) is a methodological caution, not something any retrieved passage verifies; no Neolithic jade record was successfully fetched. The corroboration museum record confirms provenience and attribution only, not meaning, material analysis or garment reconstruction.
audits.corroboration_note: Entry-cited SM record (entry line 18) fetched 2026-10-17; retrieved text: 'Kneeling-figure-shaped Jade Pendant. Date: Late Shang (13th century-1046 BCE). Dimensions: Height 5.6 cm, Width 2.8 cm. Unearthed from the tomb of Fu Hao at Xiaotun, Anyang, 1976. Henan Museum.' Verbatim agreement with entry lines 18 and 113 (excavated Fu Hao tomb context; Henan Museum object). Museum-object record: supplies Shang object evidence and provenience only; no inscription reading, garment reconstruction or symbolic meaning, so it cannot upgrade the transmitted Zhouli prescription into Shang practice.
